correctness: 400 deterministic cases across 100 seeds per objective cover all twelve study/reading/tool/file structures. Independent reconstruction checks unit conversions, affine outputs, indexed sampling intervals, grouping and decimal notation. Calculator sine/cosine are checked against a separate Taylor-series oracle on a five-degree grid, with exact inverse-sine and known-angle benchmarks. File tests verify exact field contents independent of JSON key order and formatting; malformed JSON, wrong schema, unexpected keys, mismatched marker/revision/note (including whitespace), and oversize files are rejected.
instruction: Four original lessons provide quick recall, full explanations, 16 reasoned examples, attempted guided comparison, targeted diagnostic review and an independent practical task for every objective. The retrieval source can be closed and reopened for an attempt-check-correct cycle. Scheduling examples are adaptable plans, not automatic reminders or universal ideal intervals.
tools: Local unscored calculator checks teach angle mode, inverse-sine meaning, grouping, negative bases and scientific notation. A local synthetic JSON download/reopen activity verifies note, revision and marker without replacing progress. It is explicitly distinct from the existing real progress backup.
evidence: Each practical task requires four substantive written fields, three self-check acknowledgments and a timestamp. Assistance is retained when the possible review is shown. Fresh tasks keep the last completed artifact. Confidence, visits, diagnostic and tool feedback never create numerical evidence or course completion.
persistence: Browser checks passed exact draft/seed resume, assistance persistence, fresh independent completion across all objectives, retained artifacts, ordinary notes, complete progress export/reset/import, concurrent-tab draft protection and unreadable-record recovery. Existing progress and backup schemas remain unchanged.
accessibility: All five pages passed desktop/mobile WCAG2 A/AA and WCAG2.1 AA Axe checks without overflow or KaTeX errors. Active calculator and verified-file states passed keyboard and mobile Axe checks. Desktop overview, calculator and corrected file tool were visually inspected.
sources: Eight precise free references verified: three College Success sections, three Algebra and Trigonometry 2e sections, the original Roediger/Karpicke 2006 paper on the author's institutional site, and Library of Congress personal digital records guidance. Attribution and license details are in resources.json; app prose, examples, scenarios and tools are original.
